title: The Day Is Past and Gone
description: The Day Is Past and Gone in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 951 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Evening Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The day is past and gone; Th'e-ve-ning shades ap-pear; O, may we all re-mem-ber well The night of death draws near!

lines: The day is past and gone;
O, may we all remember well
The night of death draws near!
So death shall soon disrobe us all
Lord, keep us safe this night,
May angels guard us, while we sleep,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
